values: Stellar Evolution Multiplier Rebuild — Red-Clump Variant
Every multiplier is relative to that subtype's existing MS50 reference in your simulation.
PS0 / PS1 / PS50 / PS100, then PM10 / PM50 / PM99 before ZAMS at age 2.
Most classes use core-H burning to age 70. O1 V–O4 V leave the visible main sequence at age 36 but remain core-H-burning until age 70.
Use the revised Early-BD markers. WD-forming paths now progress through month-scale late-stage windows.
The subtype does not enter that stage on this path.
For an early death, count backward from the actual death time.
No separate reference Teff, mass, or radius table is included.
Solar-metallicity, single-star, smooth simulation targets. Rotation, mass loss, metallicity and binarity can change massive-star, HB/RC and TPAGB outcomes.
HF/HeIgn is a visible settling proxy around helium ignition; it is not the instantaneous core flash.
TPAGB values represent cycle-averaged envelope states, not pulse-by-pulse maxima.
B2 V is assigned the default SAGB → ONe-WD branch. An ECSN branch can be added separately.
M1 V–M9 V now remain on the main sequence through age 105, then follow a blue-dwarf terminal path through age 117; no white-dwarf phase is assigned.

Early-radius correction: all subtype ZAMS radius multipliers were increased by 4.91% (capped at 0.995x), with PM10/PM50/PM99 recomputed for a smooth proto-MS → ZAMS transition. MS50, TAMS, and evolved-stage radii are unchanged.
Remnant rule: white dwarfs, neutron stars, black holes, and other compact remnants begin only at death; they are not living evolutionary stages in this workbook.
Post-AGB timing is simulation-compressed into the final 12 months before age 117: PostAGB10 = 12 mbd, PostAGB50 = 6 mbd, PostAGB90 = 1.2 mbd, and PostAGB100 ≈ 3.7 dbd.
No radius or Teff multiplier value was changed in this revision. PostAGB90 is a timing marker only.
Radius multipliers for O1 V through M9 V.
Individual subtype path assignment and terminal outcome.
Default ages, PostAGB90, and early-death BD markers.
Radius multipliers for O1 V through M9 V.
Effective-temperature multipliers for O1 V through M9 V.
Research sources and how they informed the rebuild.
Continuous baseClass and interpolation weights from Seeded Teff only; V is ignored.
Use the exact continuous class for calculations. Round only the final displayed class to the nearest 0.5 subtype.
General two-spectral-anchor, two-checkpoint interpolation rule for every evolutionary segment.
X1=0.92→1.00, X2=0.90→1.00, continuous class X1.662, and radius 50.65 R☉ at MS50.
Blend both checkpoint values and ages before interpolating within any segment; never reuse an anchor from another segment.
Current bound mass is normalized to ZAMS mass; every subtype has ZAMS = 1.000×.
Stage-by-stage mass multipliers for O1 V through M9 V.
Definition, interpolation order, PMS behavior, death-only remnant rule, and worked example.
Use the same Seeded-Teff and segment weights as radius/Teff; mass never determines baseClass.
B4 V–G2 V TAMS radius values were rebalanced; A and F received the strongest correction.
Mass-dependent solar-metallicity MS radius fits were blended with the existing curve and tapered at both boundaries.
ZAMS/MS50 radius, evolved radii, Teff, mass, timing, and interpolation rules were not changed.
All Seeded-Teff spectral anchors were replaced with the supplied O1–L0 temperature table.
The V suffix is ignored. Exact continuous weights are retained; only the final label rounds to the nearest 0.5.
6822.363 K now maps to F1.988185 and displays finally as F2.0.
L0 is classification-only until L0 evolution multipliers, timing, and path data are explicitly defined.

Mass Multipliers — Current Bound Mass / ZAMS Mass

Mass multiplier = current bound stellar mass ÷ ZAMS mass. ZAMS is exactly 1.000×. PMS defaults to 1.000× because no accretion prescription is included. Blank cells mean the path does not enter that stage. Compact-remnant mass is not represented because remnants begin only at death. Values are smooth, track-informed solar-metallicity simulation targets, not direct samples from one MIST track.
Each value is current bound stellar mass divided by that star's ZAMS mass.
Determine baseClass from Seeded Teff only. Mass never selects or changes baseClass.
Blend the two surrounding subtype mass multipliers with the exact Seeded-Teff weights.
Blend both mass checkpoints and their ages, then interpolate within the active segment.
PS0 through PM99 remain 1.000× unless a separate accretion model is introduced.
Single-star mass is non-increasing; interpolation must not create upward jumps.
White-dwarf, neutron-star, and black-hole masses are death-only outcomes and are not living-stage multipliers.

Research basis: MIST distinguishes initial mass, current stellar mass, and mass-loss rate in its track/isochrone outputs. The simulation therefore treats mass as its own evolving quantity rather than deriving it from radius or Teff. Massive O/WR stars receive substantial wind-driven losses; lower-mass stars retain nearly all mass on the main sequence and lose most of their envelope during RGB/AGB/TPAGB evolution. Exact mass loss remains sensitive to metallicity, rotation, wind prescriptions, and binarity.
